B- He declared that his people's only hope is God, for he said in humility that our eyes are toward You, that is, that You may rescue us.

All the people, men, women and children, in the kingdom of Judah were gathered in Jerusalem, hearing the words of Jehoshaphat's prayer with their hearts clinging to God, and because of this humility and taking refuge in God, the Lord intervenes and rescues His people and answers their prayers.

God answered Jehoshaphat's prayer quickly, so the Spirit of God came upon one of the Levites, Jahaziel, who called the people and the king and stood in their midst and asked them to listen to the word of God, which he would speak, and gave them the good news that God would lead the war, so they should not fear the enemies because of their number, for they would not fight them, but God would fight them.
The cliff of Ziz: a wilderness extending from the west of the Dead Sea to the mountains of Judah.
The wilderness of Jeruel: a desert next to the cliff of Ziz.

God commanded them, through Jahaziel, that their army should advance the next day to the cliff of Ziz, and they would find the enemies coming up toward them at the far end of this wilderness. Thus the people of God show that they are brave and going down to meet the enemies, though in truth it is God who will fight for them, so their courage is drawn from their faith in God, who answered their prayer and fasting quickly, and commanded them to face the enemies the next day.

The Lord reassured them, through Jahaziel, that they would not fight, but would stand with steadfastness and courage to see the Lord who fights for them, and not fear the enemies, because God is with them. And it is clear that they would not take weapons, but would be only spectators of the work of God and His victory, which would be accomplished. And they took with them only singers to praise God, because of their faith that God's word would certainly be carried out.

And so we see that whoever fears God and takes refuge in Him with prayer and fasting is not afraid or disturbed by any enemy, because the fear of God drives out the fear of men, and the opposite is true: whoever does not fear God trembles before men.

If you are afraid of any problems you are going through, take refuge quickly in God and trust that He is able to reassure you and defend you, so do not be disturbed by threats, or by the strength of the one who tries to wrong you. Believe and be saved.

Jehoshaphat and all the people rejoiced at the greatness of the good news, so they all bowed down before the Lord, thanking Him for His love and care, declaring their submission and obedience to all that He had said and their faith in His power, which is able to crush the enemies without their moving or doing anything. Perhaps they remembered God's words to His people in the days of Moses, before their crossing of the Red Sea (Ex 14:13).
The people expressed their joy and thanks by the Levites, of the sons of Kohath and the sons of Korah, rising to praise God and thank Him and glorify Him.

entries.section: (4) The victory over Moab, the children of Ammon and Edom

paragraphs.text: The wilderness of Tekoa: it lies southeast of Jerusalem, about 10 km away.

The people obeyed and hastened early the next day and went out to meet the enemies at the wilderness of Tekoa, with their king Jehoshaphat, who stood among them, not to prepare them for fighting, like any king or army commander when facing the enemies, but to exhort them and establish them in faith in God, for by Him they obtain reassurance, success and victory in the war, without any effort. And he stressed to them the necessity of believing everything that the prophet of God, Jahaziel, had said.

entries.section: (4) The victory over Moab, the children of Ammon and Edom

paragraphs.text: The strange thing about this war is that the army of God advances, not soldiers with experience and military skill, but a group of singers, praising God for His many mercies, as we praise Him today in the Second Hoos, in the praise of the Church.

And Jehoshaphat consulted the chiefs of the people, to encourage the army, about having a group of singers go before the army, so that they might lead the people in thanking God and strengthen their faith.

entries.section: (4) The victory over Moab, the children of Ammon and Edom

paragraphs.text: Ambushments: plural of ambush, which is a group of soldiers, hidden, who surprise the army by attacking it.

When the praise of the people of God began and their faith was established, God intervened in a miraculous way, so ambushes of soldiers moved against the armies of the enemies, and we do not know who the members of these ambushes were; they may have been angels, or the enemies may have disagreed among themselves, so ambushes of them rose against one another, that is, they divided and attacked and destroyed one another.
And God did not tell us the kind of the ambushes here, to stress the importance of faith, even if we do not know what exactly God will do.

Believe in God however impossible the solution and however complicated the matters, for He is able to save you by means that never occurred to you. Rely on Him, seek Him and let Him do what He sees fit.

entries.section: (4) The victory over Moab, the children of Ammon and Edom

paragraphs.text: Utterly destroy them: kill them.

He tells us here that the armies of the enemies rose against one another, so the Moabites and the Ammonites fought the Edomites and destroyed them, and then the Moabites and the children of Ammon fought one another, so they all perished.

entries.section: (4) The victory over Moab, the children of Ammon and Edom

paragraphs.text: The watchtower: the place from which they watch the enemies from afar.
The people of God advanced toward the valley in which the enemies had gathered, and found them all dead bodies fallen on the ground, that is, they had all perished.

entries.section: (5) The taking of the spoil and the praise of God

paragraphs.text: King Jehoshaphat and his army advanced toward the dead bodies lying in the valley, and found much spoil of money and precious goods, and they went on gathering it for three days.

entries.section: (5) The taking of the spoil and the praise of God

paragraphs.text: After the people had gathered the spoil, they assembled in a valley thirteen kilometers south of Bethlehem, and stood praising God and blessing Him, so they called the name of this valley the valley of Berachah, because they blessed God in it.

entries.section: (5) The taking of the spoil and the praise of God

paragraphs.text: After this, Jehoshaphat and his army returned with great joy to Jerusalem, because God had given them victory over their enemies by His divine power, without their fighting them, and they took much spoil from them.

entries.section: (5) The taking of the spoil and the praise of God

paragraphs.text: And on entering Jerusalem they hastened to the temple of God, and the procession was led by the singers praising God with musical instruments, such as the psalteries, the harps and the trumpets.

Jehoshaphat cared not only for praising God before the battle, but also after God's victory over them and their destroying one another, for thanking God and praising Him is the least we can offer Him after His care and protection of us. Accustom yourself to give thanks in your prayers every day, thanking Him for all that He does with you, whether great things or small.

entries.section: (5) The taking of the spoil and the praise of God

paragraphs.text: After the destruction of the armies allied against the people of God, the nations heard, so they feared God and His people. And none of them tried to fight the people of God after this, so the kingdom of Judah lived in security and rest in the days of Jehoshaphat, because of their faith and godliness.

These verses are recorded and were explained in (1 Kgs 22:42-43), and it shows in them that Jehoshaphat walked with the Lord, like Asa his father, and adds here that the people, despite their faith and godliness, were not perfect in their hearts with God, for they still offered the worship of God on the high places and not in His temple in Jerusalem. And there is a possibility that they offered worship to idols on these high places, as proved by the fact that Jehoshaphat afterwards joined with the wicked Ahaziah, king of Israel, in trade.

This verse is recorded and was explained in (1 Kgs 22:45), and we see in it that the acts of Jehoshaphat were written by Jehu the son of Hanani, in a book which is the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah, which is different from the Book of Chronicles in the Holy Bible. From this we understand that Jehu was not only a prophet but also a historian.
This incident is recorded in (1 Kgs 22:48), and is mentioned here in detail, as follows:

1- That after God's victory over the enemies of His people, Jehoshaphat sinned by going and joining with a wicked king, Ahaziah king of Israel. And the union was not in war but in trade, so he made ships for trade at Ezion-geber, to go to the cities of the world, the last of which was Tarshish.

2- God sent Eliezer the son of Dodavah the prophet, who rebuked Jehoshaphat for his union with Ahaziah, and prophesied to him that God was angry with him and would attack him. And it actually happened that these ships, which Jehoshaphat had made, were broken.

God's mercy appears from this, for He was long-suffering with Jehoshaphat, who sinned by his union with Ahaziah, so He sent him a prophet to rebuke him and his ships were broken, so Jehoshaphat repented, and refused after this to join with Ahaziah in trade, as the Book of Kings tells us (1 Kgs 22:49).
Be obedient to God's warnings and rebukes, and even to the afflictions you go through, for they bring you back to God in repentance and you hold fast to His commandments anew.
Note: see the life of Jehoshaphat at the end of the book.
Jehoram reigns over Judah

After the death of Jehoshaphat and his burial in Jerusalem, his firstborn son Jehoram reigned, whom his father had prepared to reign after him, since he shared the rule with him for the last five years of Jehoshaphat's life. Jehoram had six brothers, for whom their father Jehoshaphat cared, so he gave them authority in the cities of Judah and also gave them gifts of gold, silver and precious things, that is, valuable gifts. This was so that no dispute over the kingdom would arise after his death, for it was an implicit declaration, in Jehoshaphat's lifetime, that Jehoram was the new king, or the crown prince. Sadly Jehoram was wicked, so he feared that his brothers would compete with him for the kingdom, or take it from him, especially since they were good and better than he (2 Chr 31:13), for the people might love them and submit to one of them, who would then compete with him for the kingdom; therefore he acted with violence and cruelty and killed all his brothers, and perhaps he devised a plot and dealt treacherously with them; indeed he also killed a number of the princes of his people, who may have been good men and lovers of his brothers.

And this heinous deed that Jehoram did was widespread among the pagan nations: whoever reigns kills his brothers, lest anyone compete with him for the kingdom, and perhaps Jehoram learned this thinking from his mother-in-law, the pagan Jezebel, or from his wife Athaliah, who was influenced by her pagan mother Jezebel.

And this shows the characteristics of Jehoram, that he was not good and a lover of the Lord and His commandments, otherwise he would not have killed his innocent brothers; indeed it also shows his being influenced by his wife and his mother-in-law in the worship of idols, which he cared for, as will appear in the following verses.

Do not yield to anxiety and fear so that you become troubled, and then think evil of others, or wrong them. Rely on God and ask for His help, and He will give you peace. Enjoy His fellowship in prayer and reading, and your relationship with others will improve and you will treat them kindly.

These verses are recorded and were explained in (2 Kgs 8:16-19), and in them we see the evils of King Jehoram, which were because of his marriage to Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab king of Israel. They were many evils, deserving that God should destroy him, but He was long-suffering with him for the sake of David his forefather, the righteous king.

entries.section: (2) The revolt of Edom and Libnah against him

paragraphs.text: These verses are recorded and were explained in the Encyclopedia in (2 Kgs 8:20-22). And we see in them the Edomites' revolt against Jehoram by setting up a king over themselves, so he attacked them and triumphed over them at first, but they surrounded him, so he fled from them and the Edomites rebelled against him. Likewise the city of Libnah revolted, which lies in the kingdom of Judah and is inhabited by the priests, and God allowed this revolt because Jehoram had turned away from God and worshiped idols.

entries.section: (2) The revolt of Edom and Libnah against him

paragraphs.text: Asa, and then his son Jehoshaphat, took care of the worship of the Lord and the removal of the pagan forms of worship at the high places in the kingdom of Judah, but Jehoram did not walk in the way of his father Jehoshaphat and his forefather Asa; on the contrary, he made forms of worship for idols on the high places in the land of the kingdom of Judah. Only a group of wicked kings did this evil: Jeroboam king of Israel (1 Kgs 12:31) and Ahaz and Manasseh, kings of Judah (2 Chr 28:25, 2 Kgs 21:3). And by building these high places, Jehoram led the people of God away from His worship and cast them into the mazes of idolatry, because by this they became spiritual fornicators, by forsaking God and worshiping strange gods, and they might fall into bodily fornication to please these gods, because it was part of the rites of their worship. And in this evil in which Jehoram walked, his wife Athaliah played a great part, and also his mother-in-law Jezebel, because they were idol worshipers.

Know that every bad thought, or evil word you say, or any wicked deed, takes you away from God, so hasten to repent and do what pleases God, draw near to Him by prayer, reading the Holy Bible and every good work.

Elijah sent a letter to Jehoram king of Judah, in which he declared to him that the God of his father David was angry with him because he did not walk in the upright way in which his fathers Jehoshaphat and Asa had walked. Here he reminds him that the measure he should have set before him was his great forefather David, and then his forefather Asa and his father Jehoshaphat; he should have followed the example of their goodness, but sadly he walked in evil.

And it is important to know that Elijah went up to heaven during the life of Jehoshaphat, but in the spirit of prophecy he wrote this letter and charged his disciple Elisha the prophet to send it to Jehoram, perhaps that he would be affected by it and repent; and if he did not obey God, this letter would be a witness against him. But sadly Jehoram did not obey the word of God, so he became worse than Ahab his father-in-law, the most wicked of the kings of Israel, who did many evils, but when Elijah warned him he repented, so God postponed the punishment until after his death.
God specified to Jehoram his chief evils, which are:
1- His evil conduct like the kings of Israel, that is, the worship of idols and all the sins connected with it, such as fornication.
2- His causing his people to stumble, in turning them away from the worship of God and making them fall into the worship of idols.

3- His killing his good brothers, who were better than he, in order to rule alone; because their presence shows his sins by comparison with them, and he would be exposed to being deposed by the people. By this he shed innocent blood.

God declared his punishment to him, that he might repent and God forgive him, or so that when the punishment happened he would not think it a coincidence, but know that it was the wrath of God; but sadly he did not respond to God's warnings. And this punishment is:

1- God strikes Jehoram's wives and his sons and all that he has, and this happened at the hands of the Philistines, before Jehoram's eyes (v. 17); as he killed his brothers, God allowed his sons to be killed (ch. 22:1).
2- God strikes the wives of the people of Judah, who followed the king in the worship of idols.
3- God strikes Jehoram himself with a serious disease in his bowels, so that they come out of him while he is alive, and he dies.

And it seems that because of Jehoram's evils, which filled his heart, God allowed him to be struck in his bowels, so his bowels came out of him gradually for two years until he died (vv. 18, 19); all this is long-suffering from God, to give him an opportunity to repent.
God is wonderful in His long-suffering, for He gives us opportunity after opportunity to repent. May we seize these opportunities and return to Him, and so escape destruction.

entries.section: (4) The attack of the Philistines and the Arabs, then the death of Jehoram

paragraphs.text: The Arabs that are near the Ethiopians (Cushites): the Cushites lived in the land of Abyssinia and some of them migrated to the south of the Arabian Peninsula, that is, present-day Yemen; so the Arabs living near them are those who lived in the south of the Arabian Peninsula, that is, present-day Saudi Arabia.

Because of Jehoram's persistence in his evils, God abandoned him and allowed the Philistines and the Arabs to rise against him and attack him. How hard it is for God to be angry with a person and stir up others against him. The Philistines and the Arabs were violent, so their attack was severe.
Do not persist in your sins and so defy God, and then He abandons you, and you become an easy prey for demons and the wicked, who torment you. Hasten to repentance, for it is your only way to escape.

entries.section: (4) The attack of the Philistines and the Arabs, then the death of Jehoram

paragraphs.text: The Philistines and the Arabs attacked the kingdom of Judah and concentrated on the capital of the kingdom, so they attacked the king, and perhaps they could not kill him because of the guards who guarded him, but they entered his palaces and took his wives and sons captive, and plundered his wealth also.

And this is the natural end of the wicked, to lose everything: as he stole the share of his brothers and killed them, the wicked attacked him and plundered all his wealth, and even humbled him by taking his wives and sons.

entries.section: (4) The attack of the Philistines and the Arabs, then the death of Jehoram

paragraphs.text: After Jehoram became poor, humbled and alone, God also struck him with a serious disease, without healing, in his bowels, which began to come out of him gradually outside his body. And he was afflicted with many diseases, which continued for two years. And the diseases in the end led him to death. Thus Elijah's prophecy was fulfilled in him (v. 15). And we see the hardness of the wicked Jehoram's heart in the following:
1- Refusing to learn from the prayers of his father Jehoshaphat and his fear of God.
2- Refusing to submit to the Law of God, which his father Jehoshaphat took care to teach to all his people.

3- Refusing to submit to Elijah's letter and warnings, and perhaps Athaliah his wife encouraged him in this, and she may have burned this letter with contempt and scorn, and kept him away from the Law of God and from praying to Him.

4- After Elijah's prophecy was fulfilled in him, and it was in stages, his heart was not affected and he did not return to God, for his wealth was plundered and his wives and sons were taken captive, then the disease struck him and continued for two years, and in all this he refused to repent, so he died and went to destruction.

Because of Jehoram's evils his people did not love him, because whoever kills his brothers is of course a person of utmost selfishness and cruelty, and consequently is cruel and unjust to his people. And the people, especially the good among them, would have preferred that one of Jehoram's good brothers reign over them, who were influenced by the goodness of Jehoshaphat and his prayer and teachings, and were troubled by Jehoram's spreading of the worship of idols. All this made them feel distress at Jehoram, so when he died they did not make an honor for him like the rest of the kings; they did not make for him the great burning, in which they used to put spices, which gave a pleasant sight and fragrance, because Jehoram's life was evil and foul and had nothing good in it, so they did not mourn his death.

entries.section: (4) The attack of the Philistines and the Arabs, then the death of Jehoram

paragraphs.text: Jehoram reigned alone on the throne when he was thirty-two years old and reigned for eight years, but he had also reigned five years before that with his father Jehoshaphat, so the total of his reign was thirteen years (2 Kgs 8:16). And he died at about forty years old. And because of the people's distress at him, they buried him in the city of David, but did not bury him in the tombs of the kings his fathers, although there were wicked kings before him, such as Rehoboam and Abijah, but Jehoram's evils were greater than theirs, so they did not bury him with them. And this signifies the separation of the wicked from the righteous at the end of the days, that is, the wicked will be separated and cast into eternal torment.
Ahaziah, and then Athaliah, reign over Judah

entries.section: (3) The death of Jehoiada and Joash's apostasy from the Lord

paragraphs.text: God prolonged the life of Jehoiada, so he lived longer than was usual in his days, for he lived 130 years, and so he was born in the days of King Solomon and lived in the time of nine kings, the first of whom was Solomon and the last Joash, and he enjoyed the goodness that prevailed in the days of Asa and Jehoshaphat. All this was a preparation by God for him, to play a great role, which was the care of the child king Joash, whom he raised when he was one year old, then crowned and anointed king when he was seven years old, and continued to care for him and guide him, so he worshiped the Lord and carried out the restoration of the temple, so that he even reproached Jehoiada himself for his lack of zeal in collecting silver for the restoration of the temple. Although Jehoiada had some excuse, because his age at that time was nearly 130 years. Thus the importance of the priestly role in the Book of Chronicles appears, because the goodness in the first part of the life of King Joash is owed to Jehoiada

entries.section: (3) The death of Jehoiada and Joash's apostasy from the Lord

paragraphs.text: In honor of the great Jehoiada, to whom is owed the goodness of the kingdom in the days of Joash, and perhaps his goodness preserved the temple even in the days of the wicked kings; therefore they buried him with honor in the city of David beside the kings, and perhaps they wrote on his tomb that he "did good with God and His house," so they distinguished him by burying him with the kings.

entries.section: (3) The death of Jehoiada and Joash's apostasy from the Lord

paragraphs.text: After the death of Jehoiada a group of the princes of Judah came to King Joash, whose minds were corrupted and who loved the worship of idols, and they are those who lived in the days of Jehoram, Ahaziah and Athaliah, the wicked kings. And they showed their submission to the king by bowing down to him, and perhaps they flattered him; indeed they showed him that he had been rid of the high priest, who had controlled him, and that he was free now to do what he saw fit and to seek help from the other gods and benefit from them, as all the nations around him worship them. And they continued in their talk until they convinced him, so he agreed to establish the worship of idols, by offering worship at the groves and the images of idols, and they neglected the worship of the Lord, so the Lord was angry with them.

entries.section: (3) The death of Jehoiada and Joash's apostasy from the Lord

paragraphs.text: God was long-suffering with His people in the kingdom of Judah and sent them prophets to guide them and bring them back to God, but sadly they rejected the word of God and continued in their evil and their worship of idols. This shows that God does not leave Himself without a witness, and also shows the people's persistence and insistence on evil.

entries.section: (3) The death of Jehoiada and Joash's apostasy from the Lord

paragraphs.text: God also warned His people through Zechariah the priest the son of Jehoiada, for the Spirit of God came upon him, and he stood on a high platform, so he was higher than all the people, and called to all who were gathered that they should turn from the worship of idols and worship God, and he showed the extent of their evil and their betrayal of God, and warned them that their forsaking God would expose them to God's abandoning them and consequently failure in all their life. And this warning of his is from the Law of God (Deut 29:25, 31:16, 17), that is, he conveyed the word of God to them so that they might repent.
And perhaps this Zechariah is the one mentioned in the New Testament, of whom Christ said that he was Zechariah the son of Barachias (Mt 23:35), because Jehoiada is also called Barachias.

entries.section: (3) The death of Jehoiada and Joash's apostasy from the Lord

paragraphs.text: When the wicked princes and the people, who clung to the worship of idols, heard the words of Zechariah, they reported him to King Joash, since he had transgressed his commands and was teaching the people against the king's words, so Joash commanded that Zechariah be killed, and they stoned him while he was teaching in the court of the house of the Lord. And this shows the extent of the evil to which Joash descended, so that he became a resister of the word of God and was led to the worship of idols.

entries.section: (3) The death of Jehoiada and Joash's apostasy from the Lord

paragraphs.text: Joash's killing of Zechariah shows his betrayal of God and his lack of appreciation for the kindness of Jehoiada, who raised him and preserved him, instead of his dying at the hand of Athaliah, and indeed crowned him king and guided him in the administration of the kingdom, so he succeeded and worshiped the Lord.

And at the death of Zechariah he said in the spirit of prophecy, "The LORD look upon it, and require it." He does not want God's vengeance on them, but rebukes them in the last moments of his life, perhaps they would repent, but sadly they refused to hear the word of God, so only a year passed and the Arameans attacked and triumphed over them, and the Lord struck Joash with disease. And what confirms that Zechariah's words are a prophecy that was fulfilled more than once is that Christ Himself referred to Zechariah and God's requiring his blood when He said, "All the righteous blood shed upon the earth shall come upon this generation, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar" (Mt 23:35).

God moved Zechariah to alert the people to the words of the Law so that they would repent. And God alerts you in many ways so that you return to Him, so do not persist in your sins and reject the word of God, because He loves you and seeks your salvation.

entries.section: (4) The attack of the Arameans and the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: At the end of the year: after about a year.

After the prophecy of Zechariah the son of Jehoiada, at his death, only a year passed and the armies of the Arameans attacked the kingdom of Judah and killed the princes of the people, who had turned King Joash toward the worship of idols, and then plundered everything precious in Judah and Jerusalem and sent it to the capital of their king, Damascus.

And so we see God's abandoning His rebellious people, so He allows the killing of the wicked princes of the people and the plundering of the spoil of the kingdom, that His people may become poor, perhaps by this they would repent and return to God.

entries.section: (4) The attack of the Arameans and the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: A small company: a small group.
They executed judgment: they ruled and humbled and punished.

To declare His severe abandoning of His people, God allowed a small number of Arameans to attack, and a great army from the kingdom of Judah confronted them but was defeated before them, because God wanted to punish the kingdom of Judah by the hand of their enemies the Arameans, and to humble His people He made them be defeated before a small group. And this is the opposite of God's work with His people when they hold fast to Him, as He was with them in the days of Jehoshaphat, when they triumphed over a huge army of the alliance of the Moabites, the Ammonites and the Edomites, without fighting them (ch. 20:20-25).

The power of God is available to you, if you believe in it and hold fast to God's commandments, but if you rebel against God and neglect His commandments, He abandons you, and the wicked despise you and humble you. Why do you give up your standing as the king's son? Rise quickly and return to God, to regain your sonship.

entries.section: (4) The attack of the Arameans and the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: After the Arameans plundered Jerusalem and the king's palace, they found Joash sick with severe diseases, so they left him.

And as a punishment from God, two of Joash's servants rose against him and killed him while he was asleep on his bed. And this punishment was because of his killing innocent souls, the sons of Jehoiada: Zechariah the priest and his brothers. And this shows the extent of Joash's cruelty and his plunging into the worship of idols, and consequently his deserving the severe punishment that came upon him and his kingdom and his wicked princes. And God punished the whole kingdom, because they strayed from God and worshiped idols. And when the people felt the evil that had come upon them because of Joash, they did not bury him, when he died, in the tombs of the kings, but buried him with the common people, in the city of David.

It is noticed that the two killers of the king were of Gentile origin, that is, of the offspring of Moab and the children of Ammon, and this shows the extent of the spread of marriages contrary to the Law, that is, marrying Gentile women, so the king deserved this punishment.

entries.section: (4) The attack of the Arameans and the death of Joash

paragraphs.text: The burdens laid upon him: what God punished him with, or the punishment that came upon him.
Midrash: a book of interpretation containing sermons.

The rest of the acts of King Joash and of his sons, and the divine punishments that came upon him, and all the accounts of his restoration of the house of the Lord, were written in the book of the Book of Kings, which is a historical book different from the Book of Kings that is in the Holy Bible; then his son Amaziah reigned on the throne of Judah after the death of his father Joash. Amaziah king of Judah

entries.section: (2) The victory over Edom and Amaziah's apostasy

paragraphs.text: Amaziah prepared to fight Edom, and the men of his army succeeded, numbering 300,000 warriors trained for war. This number is small compared with the army of the kingdom of Judah about fifty years earlier, in the days of his grandfather Jehoshaphat, when they numbered about one million two hundred thousand (2 Chr 17:14-18). The smallness of the army may be due to the absence of God's blessing, because most of the kings after Jehoshaphat were wicked. But why did Amaziah prepare to fight Edom? Perhaps Edom threatened war, or gathered armies on the border, so Amaziah was forced to prepare for war, and he found his army small. What would he do? This will appear in the next verse.

entries.section: (2) The victory over Edom and Amaziah's apostasy

paragraphs.text: A talent of silver: The talent had different weights, ranging between 17 and 40 kg.

Amaziah sought the help of mercenary soldiers to assist him in the war, and he paid for them a hundred talents of silver. They were from the tribe of Ephraim, from the kingdom of Israel, since this tribe was large and known for its military strength.

entries.section: (2) The victory over Edom and Amaziah's apostasy

paragraphs.text: God's love appeared in His sending a prophet, whose name is not mentioned, who declared to King Amaziah that he should not take help from the army of the kingdom of Israel, because they were wicked, worshipping idols, and God was not with them, and it is not right to take help from the wicked. By this the prophet showed Amaziah the weakness of his faith, because he did not trust in God, who helps the weak, but went to trust in men, and even in the wicked.

entries.section: (2) The victory over Edom and Amaziah's apostasy

paragraphs.text: The prophet asked Amaziah to go alone, and God would support him, however weak he was; but if he trusted in the wicked, he would be defeated and fall, whereas if he trusted in God, he would surely be victorious, because victory is by the power of the Lord.

At the beginning of the verse God plainly commands Amaziah to be strong and to go alone to fight; the second part shows him that he will fall if he goes with the army of Israel; then in the third part of the verse it returns to show that God has the power to help, so Amaziah does not need the help of the wicked.

entries.section: (2) The victory over Edom and Amaziah's apostasy

paragraphs.text: Amaziah felt a great loss if he did not take an army from the tribe of Ephraim, because he had already paid the sum of 100 talents of silver. He was ready to obey God, but he was thinking of the large sum that he had paid and had not benefited from. Here the prophet answered him that God is able to compensate him for this sum, but he must carry out God's word and not take help from the wicked.

entries.section: (2) The victory over Edom and Amaziah's apostasy

paragraphs.text: Amaziah's obedience to God appeared in his dismissing the army of Ephraim and accepting the loss of the huge sum he had paid them, which was a hundred talents. On the other hand, the army of Ephraim murmured bitterly against Amaziah, for they considered their dismissal an insult and a sign that they were not needed, that is, that they were weak and worthless, and they departed in great anger, planning to take revenge on Amaziah and to punish him for this insult. Perhaps they were also angry because, by not entering the war, they were deprived of the spoils which they had hoped to obtain from the enemies, and this shows the extent of their pride, since they did not think of the possibility of their being defeated before the enemies and of some of them dying.

Be obedient to God's commandments, even if you are alone in carrying out the commandments; and do not be troubled by the threats of the wicked, for all this is worthless, because God supports you, and no man can prevail against you.

entries.section: (2) The victory over Edom and Amaziah's apostasy

paragraphs.text: The Valley of Salt: A valley south of the Dead Sea and beside it.
The children of Seir: The Edomites, the descendants of Esau, who dwell in the mountains of Seir.

After Amaziah obeyed God, he advanced with courage and faith, and was able to defeat the armies of the Edomites, and even killed 10,000 warriors of them at the place of the battle, which is the Valley of Salt.

entries.section: (2) The victory over Edom and Amaziah's apostasy

paragraphs.text: The rock (Sela): A fortified stronghold in the mountains of Seir, which the Edomites inhabit, and it lies near the foot of one of their mountains, which is called Mount Hor.

Amaziah was dazzled by the fortifications of the Edomites and their mountains, and also their temples, in which they offered human sacrifices; so when he triumphed over them, he imitated their savagery and threw 10,000 of the Edomites, whom he had taken captive, from the top of a fortified stronghold of theirs called the rock (Sela), and they fell dead from the mountain; and this method was known among the savage Edomites.

entries.section: (2) The victory over Edom and Amaziah's apostasy

paragraphs.text: Beth-horon: Two cities, one of them built on a plateau and called Upper Beth-horon, and the other in the valley and called Lower Beth-horon, and they lie on the border between the two kingdoms of Israel and Judah, that is, between the tribes of Ephraim and Benjamin.
Samaria: The capital of the kingdom of Israel, and it lies north of Jerusalem at a distance of 40 miles, and east of the Mediterranean at a distance of 25 miles.

As a result of the anger of the army of Ephraim, whom Amaziah had dismissed, they attacked the kingdom of Judah on its northern borders, taking advantage of the army of Judah's having gone to fight the Edomites, who dwell south of Judah; and they killed three thousand from the kingdom of Judah and plundered much spoil.

God permitted this attack on the kingdom of Judah because Amaziah's heart was not perfectly upright; for although he obeyed God, he admired the wicked Edomites and their idols, as will appear from the following verses.

entries.section: (2) The victory over Edom and Amaziah's apostasy

paragraphs.text: Amaziah's evil appeared in his apostasy from God, and he did not stop at admiring the idolaters, but regarded their idols as a great spoil, so he took these images and carried them to Jerusalem and set them up there and bowed down and offered worship to them.

This great apostasy shows that Amaziah was superficial in his relationship with God, so at his first test he fell, for he loved the worship of idols. Perhaps the motive for this was his pride, because he had triumphed over the Edomites, and pride darkens the mind. So he took the idols which were not able to protect those who worshipped them, in order to rely on these strange gods and bow down to them instead of God.

This shows the extent of the influence of pagan gods on man, for although Amaziah was able to obey God and give up the love of money in the form of the hundred talents of silver, he did not stand before the allurement of the pagan images, but carried them with admiration to Jerusalem and submitted to them.

entries.section: (2) The victory over Edom and Amaziah's apostasy

paragraphs.text: God was angry because of Amaziah's apostasy and sent him a prophet who rebuked him, because he submitted to and worshipped the feeble idols which were not able to protect the Edomites who worshipped them. How could he be dazzled by them? And instead of giving thanks to God in His temple because He had given him victory over the enemies, he bowed down to the feeble pagan gods, that is, to the demons who work in them.

entries.section: (2) The victory over Edom and Amaziah's apostasy

paragraphs.text: Amaziah refused to listen to the voice of God from the mouth of the prophet and interrupted him, saying to him, "Be silent," and even threatened him with death, as he had formerly killed Zechariah the son of Jehoiada, whom God had sent to Joash his father. Here this prophet completed his message to Amaziah and said to him that, because of his refusal to hear the voice of God, he had condemned himself to certain death and destruction on account of his sin.

What happened with Amaziah shows that he was in a crisis and in fear of Edom; therefore he obeyed the first prophet, but when he triumphed he became proud and felt that he had no need of God, so he rejected the voice of the second prophet.
Gath: One of the five great cities of the Philistines, which are Gath, Ekron, Ashkelon, Ashdod and Gaza, and it lies on the coast of the Mediterranean, north of Ashdod, at a distance of 12 miles.
Jabneh: A large city in Palestine, lying south of Joppa, at a distance of 20 km.
Ashdod: One of the five great cities of the Philistines, lying north of Gaza, at a distance of 30 km, and it is midway between Gaza and Joppa.

The Philistines submitted to King Jehoshaphat and brought him gifts (ch. 17:11), but they took advantage of the weakness of Jehoram his son, because of his departure from God, and attacked him, and took his wives, his children and his possessions (ch. 21:16). But when Uzziah relied on God, he fought the Philistines, who dwell south of the kingdom of Judah toward the coast of the Mediterranean, and attacked three of their great cities, which are Gath, Jabneh and Ashdod, and broke down their walls and took them, and was even able also to build cities belonging to him in those regions. This was his first success.
Gur-baal: A region inhabited by Arabs, lying south of Beersheba, that is, south of the kingdom of Judah, and it used to worship Baal, so it was called by this name.

The Mehunims: A tribe of the Edomites dwelling in the mountains of Seir, which lie south of the kingdom of Judah. The second success which Uzziah achieved was his victory over other places of the Philistines and the Arabs dwelling in Gur-baal and the Mehunims dwelling in the mountains of Seir. And when the Ammonites submitted to him, they gave him gifts to appease him. The influence and authority of Uzziah extended to the borders of Egypt, that is, he gained greatness and power, so all the nations feared him, until he reached the borders of the mighty kingdom of Egypt.
The corner gate: It lies in the northwest of the city of Jerusalem.
The valley gate: It lies in the southwest of the city of Jerusalem.

Uzziah's third success was his fortifying of Jerusalem, for he built towers in the wall of Jerusalem, at the corner gate and the valley gate, that is, he rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem, which Joash king of Israel had broken down in his war with Amaziah, the father of Uzziah (2 Chr 26:9).
Carmel: Its meaning is the fruitful garden, and it is a fertile land lying south of the kingdom of Judah.

Uzziah's fourth success was his building of towers in the wilderness of Judah, and his digging of wells to help in the grazing and care of the sheep, because he owned much cattle in the valleys of Judah and as far as the coast of the Mediterranean. And Uzziah's fifth success was his attention to agriculture, for he loved it, so he cared for the various crops in the fertile lands of his kingdom, such as Carmel and in many places of the kingdom, and he had many farmers who tended these crops.
Bands: Divisions.
The ruler: An officer of high rank.

Uzziah's sixth success was his forming a large army whose number was three hundred and seven thousand five hundred soldiers (307,500 soldiers), and they were divided into divisions, so they moved in order, under the command of the king's scribe and two of his military commanders. It is understood from this that Uzziah established a new system and divided his army into divisions, so that they would go out to war company by company according to this system, while the other companies remained to protect the state in careful order. Uzziah was a military thinker, distinguished from the kings who preceded him.
And he had two thousand six hundred commanders who led his great army.
Shields: The plural of shield, a defensive weapon consisting of a piece of wood.
Helmets: The plural of helmet, a metal covering placed on the head of the fighting soldier to protect it.
Habergeons: The plural of habergeon, a metal garment which the warrior wears on his chest down to his knees.
Bows: The plural of bow, by which arrows are shot.
Slings: The plural of sling, a leather instrument in which small stones are placed to be hurled far away and strike the enemies, as David did with Goliath.
Engines: The plural of engine (catapult), an ancient war machine with which stones and balls of fire are thrown to break down the walls of cities and burn them.

Uzziah was concerned to arm his army with various weapons, whether for the individual warrior, to defend him, such as shields and habergeons, or for attacking the enemies, such as spears and bows and slings. Likewise the great war machines, such as catapults, which had been invented at a time before Uzziah, but he took care to develop them by means of inventors from his army, that is, he had an army armed with the latest weapons.

Uzziah was distinguished by many talents, and he succeeded in all fields, as we mentioned in the previous verses, so that his knowledge, skill and strength spread and people spoke of them among the nations around him, like Solomon his forefather, because the power of God that helped him appeared wonderful and mighty in the eyes of all, and he became strong and successful in all that he did. But unfortunately he fell into pride after this, and made himself a priest, and dared to enter the sanctuary, where none enters but the priests, so the Lord struck him with leprosy and he was separated from the people because of his uncleanness, as will appear in the following verses of this chapter.

When the grace of God given to you increases, may your heart be lifted up with abundant thanksgiving, lest Satan deceive you and you think that you are something and become proud toward people and God, and so lose everything.

entries.section: (3) The sin, leprosy and death of Uzziah

paragraphs.text: When God blessed King Uzziah and he became strong and prospered in the various fields of administering the kingdom, he became proud and did not ascribe the glory to God, but felt that he was an outstanding king and could do everything, so that he dared to consider that he had the right to enter the sanctuary, like the rest of the priests, and he entered to burn incense on the altar of incense, before the Holy of Holies.

entries.section: (3) The sin, leprosy and death of Uzziah

paragraphs.text: The high priest, who was Azariah, was taken by surprise at Uzziah's bursting into the sanctuary, and he was very angry, and so were all the priests with him who were serving in the temple, so Azariah entered after Uzziah with eighty priests, to bring him out of the sanctuary. They commanded him to go out of the sanctuary and informed him that it was not his right to enter, since he was not a priest (Ex 30:7, Deut 33:10). But unfortunately he did not listen to the warnings of the priests not to enter, and perhaps he felt that the prohibition of entering applied to the people but did not apply to him, since the king, in his view, is greater than the priests.

It is clear that Uzziah forgot what happened to Korah and his company, who dared to assume the priesthood in the days of Moses and Aaron, so the earth split open and swallowed them (Num 16:35). It is understood from this that Uzziah wanted to combine the dignity of the king and the dignity of the priesthood in his person, and this was not his right, and no one can combine these two dignities except Christ Himself, who is King of kings and the High Priest of the New Covenant, who offered the sacrifice of Himself on the Cross.

entries.section: (3) The sin, leprosy and death of Uzziah

paragraphs.text: Wroth: Became violently angry or enraged.

King Uzziah was enraged because of the priests' command to him to go out of the sanctuary, for, because of his pride, he was not accustomed to anyone's commanding him; everyone must submit to him, but he submits to no one. Uzziah had taken hold of a censer to burn incense on the altar of incense, like the priests, and since he did not submit to God and resisted in rebellion, God struck him with leprosy immediately, and a white spot appeared on his forehead, so the priests drove him out of the sanctuary, and he himself was very afraid, for he knew that he had been struck with leprosy and had become unclean from the Lord, and that he must be set apart, not only from the temple, but from all the people.

The historian Josephus says that the earthquake which occurred in the days of Uzziah and is mentioned in (Amos 1:1) and (Zech 14:5) took place at this time, when Uzziah was struck with leprosy. Josephus also says that the roof of the temple split open and a ray of the sun entered and fell on the face of Uzziah, so his leprosy appeared plainly before all the priests, which made them drive him quickly out of the temple, and Uzziah was in great terror.

Uzziah tried in pride to seize the dignity of the priesthood alongside the dignity of the kingship, but he lost both, just as Adam and Eve tried to obtain new knowledge apart from God by eating of the forbidden tree, and so lost their place in Paradise and their knowledge of God.

We see Uzziah becoming proud and rebelling against the priests in his entering the sanctuary, but God struck him with leprosy, so he came under the authority of the priests, who examined him and found him a leper, and drove him out and set him apart.

Pride makes man lose his true dignity, so that he becomes despised and rejected by God, and the angels and saints grieve over him. Therefore your humility and your thanksgiving to God protect you from the fall of the proud devil, and you will be able to taste the love of God.

entries.section: (3) The sin, leprosy and death of Uzziah

paragraphs.text: The priests set Uzziah apart in a house by himself, which they called the house of sickness, in which those afflicted with the disease of leprosy are confined, and he remained afflicted with this disease until the end of his life. Perhaps this was a proof of his uncleanness and of God's rejection of him, and consequently he could not mingle with the people, so his son Jotham reigned in his place, and thus Uzziah, who had been proud, was humbled, so that all the people might know the seriousness of pride.

entries.section: (3) The sin, leprosy and death of Uzziah

paragraphs.text: The rest of the acts and life of Uzziah were written by Isaiah the prophet, who was his contemporary. Then Uzziah died, and they did not honor him like the rest of the kings, but buried him in the field of the burial ground of the kings, because he was unclean with his leprosy; then Jotham reigned alone after the death of his father, because he had been reigning for a long time with his father during his sickness.
Jotham reigns over Judah

These verses were mentioned and explained in (2 Kgs 15:33), and in them we see that Jotham became king at the age of twenty-five and reigned sixteen years, and his mother's name was Jerushah the daughter of Zadok. It seems that she was devout, so she brought up her son well, and he walked uprightly.

Jotham walked in uprightness and goodness, like his father, but he learned from his father's mistake, so he respected the priesthood and feared God and worshipped Him with reverence. But he was lenient with his people, so he left them to be corrupted by the worship of idols on the high places, that is, he did not remove the high places and the idols on them. Isaiah portrayed this corruption in his prophecy (Isa 1-5), and so did the prophet Micah in his prophecy (1:9, 2:2, 3:8-10, 3:1-2, 5-12).
Ophel: A quarter inside Jerusalem lying to its southwest and to the southwest of the temple, and it connects the king's gardens with the temple.

Although Jotham did not prevent his people from pagan worship on the high places, he tried in a positive way to draw them to the worship of God, for he took care to build a great gate for the temple, called the higher gate, and by this Jotham fortified the temple.
Jotham's concern extended to fortifying Jerusalem, so he built the ruined wall of the city, which was on the side of Ophel.
Jotham loved building works, like his father Uzziah, so he took care to build cities in the kingdom of Judah, and he also built towers and fortresses to fortify and protect the city and those in it.
A talent of silver: It has several weights, from 17 to 40 kg.

Measures (cors): A measure for grain equal to 229 liters. Jotham's strength appeared in his great army, and God helped him because of his uprightness, so he fought the children of Ammon, who dwell east of his kingdom, and triumphed over them and subdued them, so that they paid him a great tribute, whose value was a hundred talents of silver, as well as ten thousand measures of wheat and ten thousand of barley. And the Ammonites continued to pay him this tribute annually for two more years.
Jotham reached this strength in his building works and his wars because he walked uprightly before the Lord.
If you please God by your upright conduct, He blesses you and makes your works prosper and protects you from the wars of the devil, so He gives you victory over him and you live in peace.
(2) The end of Jotham (vv. 7-9).
7- Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all his wars, and his ways, lo, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

8- He was five and twenty years old when he began to reign, and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. 9- And Jotham slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David: and Ahaz his son reigned in his stead. These verses were mentioned and explained in (2 Kgs 15:36, 38), and in them we see the death of Jotham and his burial in the city of David, and then the reign of Ahaz his son.

However great a position a person holds on earth, he will leave it by death. Therefore take care to prepare for your eternal life, by keeping God's commandments and doing good, so that you may have a great place in heaven.
Ahaz reigns over Judah

entries.section: (1) Ahaz's corruption and his defeat before Aram and Israel

paragraphs.text: These verses were mentioned and explained in (2 Kgs 16:1-4), and in them we see Ahaz's corruption, his abandoning the worship of God and his immersion in the worship of idols.

entries.section: (1) Ahaz's corruption and his defeat before Aram and Israel

paragraphs.text: Ahaz fell into the worship of idols without any cause, because his father was upright and left him much money in the treasury of the kingdom, since he had triumphed over the surrounding enemies, such as the children of Ammon. Therefore God abandoned Ahaz and let the king of Aram attack him and kill many of his people, because they too had gone astray after the king in the worship of idols.
God also permitted the king of Israel to attack him and kill many of his people and take many captives.

What is mentioned in (2 Kgs 16:5, 6), that the king of Aram and the king of Israel did not overcome Ahaz, means that they wanted to depose and kill him and appoint another king instead of him, but they were not able to do so, yet they killed many of his people. And God did not permit the deposing of Ahaz, because He had promised that a descendant of David would remain on his throne forever. And He sent Isaiah to Ahaz and reassured him that God would keep him (Isa 7).

entries.section: (1) Ahaz's corruption and his defeat before Aram and Israel

paragraphs.text: Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, killed a great number of the mighty soldiers of Ahaz, numbering 120,000, because of the kingdom of Judah's walking in evil.

entries.section: (1) Ahaz's corruption and his defeat before Aram and Israel

paragraphs.text: And Zichri, the commander of the army of Israel, was able to reach the royal palace and kill Maaseiah the son of Ahaz, and he also killed Azrikam, who was over the royal palace, and Elkanah, the second man in the kingdom after Ahaz.

Thus God punished Ahaz by the killing of his son and his helpers and a great number of his army, that perhaps he might repent and return to God. And although Ahaz had offered his son as a sacrifice to the idols, here another son of his dies by the sword; for whoever walks in evil will find before him nothing but divine punishment.

Do not challenge God by persisting in evil, lest He be angry with you and abandon you, and the demons humiliate you and those around you trouble you. Return to Him with repentance. He is compassionate and will forgive you.

entries.section: (2) Israel's captivity of Judah and its return

paragraphs.text: The army of Israel was able to take captive 200,000 of the people of Judah, men, women and children, and they plundered much spoil from them. Thus Judah was humbled because of its sins. And although Ahaz had admired the pagan gods whom Israel worshipped and followed them in the worship of idols, now God stirs up the king of Israel against him, to kill and take captive many of his people, in order to teach him not to follow sinners or imitate them in their sins.

entries.section: (2) Israel's captivity of Judah and its return

paragraphs.text: God's compassion appears toward the inhabitants of the kingdom of Judah, who had rebelled against Him by worshipping idols. For after the kingdom of Israel took them captive, He sent a prophet named Oded to the capital of Israel, which is Samaria, to meet the army of Israel returning with the captives of Judah and its spoil, and he declared to them the following:
1- God disciplined the inhabitants of Judah for their sins, so they were defeated in the war before Israel.

2- The prophet Oded reminded Israel that they had many sins, and that God was longsuffering toward them, but He would abandon them and discipline them if they did not repent; so how could they take captives and spoil from their brethren, the inhabitants of Judah?
3- If Israel had many sins, let it have compassion on its brethren of Judah, sinners like itself, and return their captives to their land.

entries.section: (2) Israel's captivity of Judah and its return

paragraphs.text: The inhabitants of Samaria were moved by the words of Oded and felt their sins and returned to God. So four of the chiefs of Israel rose up, followed by the people, and spoke to the heads of the army who were returning to Samaria with the captives, and reminded them that Israel had many sins which deserved the divine wrath, so it was not right for us to add to them a new sin, which is cruelty to our brethren the people of Judah, by taking them captive to Israel.

This turning and submission to God is a matter that gladdens God, so that He took care to mention the names of the four chiefs in the Holy Bible, though they are not mentioned except in this place. It resembles the goodness shown by the good Samaritan in the parable told by Christ (Lk 10:29-37). For God does not forget the goodness and service of any person, and He cares for everyone who obeys Him and bears witness to Him, especially among the wicked.

entries.section: (2) Israel's captivity of Judah and its return

paragraphs.text: The heads of the army obeyed the chiefs of Israel, so they left before them the captives from Judah and all their spoil.

entries.section: (2) Israel's captivity of Judah and its return

paragraphs.text: The chiefs of Israel appointed a number of the people of Israel to care for the captives, and this care appeared in the following:
1- They took clothes from the spoil and clothed the naked captives.
2- They took suitable sandals from the spoil and put them on all the captives.
3- They gave them food and drink, because they had been hungry and thirsty for some time.

4- They cared for the wounds which had afflicted them while they were being seized, or beaten, and while being dragged and carried to Samaria, so they anointed their wounds with oil that they might heal.
5- They cared for those of them who were weary and unable to walk, and set them on donkeys, so that they would not fall on the way back to their country.

6- They led them with gentleness and love and looked after them during their journey, until they brought them to the city of Jericho, which is called the city of palm trees, a city lying in the north of the kingdom of Judah.
In these steps we see wonderful care on the part of the Samaritans, which resembles, as we said, what the good Samaritan did.
Be merciful and have compassion on the weary around you, because your tenderness toward them is very precious in the sight of God, and He pours out His mercies upon you.

entries.section: (3) Ahaz's brokenness before Edom, Philistia and Assyria

paragraphs.text: After Ahaz's crushing defeat before Aram and Israel, he did not think of returning to God, but tried to seek the help of a great state, Assyria, which dwells in the north of present-day Iraq, to help him against Aram and all the enemies around him. This shows the extent of Ahaz's hardness of heart and his distance from God.

entries.section: (3) Ahaz's brokenness before Edom, Philistia and Assyria

paragraphs.text: God continued His discipline of the hard-hearted Ahaz, so He permitted Edom, who dwells south of Judah, to attack Ahaz, and it triumphed over him and took captives from him.

entries.section: (3) Ahaz's brokenness before Edom, Philistia and Assyria

paragraphs.text: Beth-shemesh: A city in the north of the kingdom of Judah and on its border.
Ajalon: A city on the border of the kingdom of Judah in its north, lying west of Jerusalem at a distance of 22 km. Gederoth: A city in the plain of Judah.

Shocho: A city in the plain of Judah, lying southwest of Bethlehem, at a distance of 14 miles. Timnah: A city lying on the northern border of Judah, 5 km southwest of Beth-shemesh. Gimzo: A village lying southeast of Lydda at a distance of 5 km.
God also permitted the Philistines to attack the kingdom of Judah from its south and its north, and they seized a number of its cities.

entries.section: (3) Ahaz's brokenness before Edom, Philistia and Assyria

paragraphs.text: Made Judah unruly: He made Judah rebel against God.

Ahaz led his people in rebellion against God and made them wander in the worship of idols, so God permitted him and his people to be disciplined, and humbled him before the nations around him. For after he became weak before Aram and Israel, the other nations around Ahaz, such as Edom and Philistia, seized the opportunity, so they attacked him and seized his cities and took captives from him. In all this Ahaz did not repent and take refuge in God, but sought the nations and their gods, such as Assyria.

entries.section: (3) Ahaz's brokenness before Edom, Philistia and Assyria

paragraphs.text: Then, in continuation of God's humbling of Ahaz, He permitted Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, whom Ahaz had tried to enlist for help, but who did not support him, to attack him and humble him, although he had taken from Ahaz many gifts, from the house of the Lord, from the king's palace and from the princes of Judah. And because Ahaz stripped the house of the Lord of its contents and gave them as gifts to the king of Assyria, the king of Assyria did not help him, but increased his humiliation and weakness.

Do not take refuge in the world, lest it humble you, but seek God your compassionate Father, because however much you sin, He is ready to forgive you as long as you return to Him. Leave the means of the world, its lusts and wrong ways, to save your soul from perishing.

entries.section: (4) Ahaz's worship of the gods of Assyria and his death

paragraphs.text: Although affliction calls man to return to God, when God permitted affliction to come upon Ahaz, he drew away from God and clung to the nations and their idols.

entries.section: (4) Ahaz's worship of the gods of Assyria and his death

paragraphs.text: In Ahaz's persistence in his evil, he took refuge in the gods of Aram, who had smitten and humbled him, and did not take refuge in God. He feared the gods of Aram and sought their help, although God is the greatest power in the world, but in his ignorance Ahaz rejected God.

entries.section: (4) Ahaz's worship of the gods of Assyria and his death

paragraphs.text: Ahaz cut in pieces the large vessels which were in the house of the Lord, to send them as metal gifts to Assyria, and he shut up the house of the Lord and prevented service in it. He most likely shut up the sanctuary and the Holy of Holies, that is, he prevented the priests from entering and offering service to God, because he had set up an altar for the idols, like what he had seen in Damascus among the Arameans; that is, he prevented the worship of God and encouraged the worship of idols, and moreover he set up altars for the idols in every corner of the city of Jerusalem.

Persisting in sin blinds a person's eyes, so that he departs from the truth. Therefore be careful to pray, to read the Holy Bible and to receive Holy Communion, so that your relationship with God may remain alive.

entries.section: (4) Ahaz's worship of the gods of Assyria and his death

paragraphs.text: Likewise Ahaz established the worship of idols in the cities of Judah, and not in Jerusalem only, and by this he provoked God and greatly angered Him, because he led his people astray and led them far from God.

Thus we see Ahaz's evil in that he spread the worship of idols, set up the high places and shut up the house of God. He was not merely lenient with his people in the worship of idols, but encouraged them in this wicked worship and drew them away from God.

entries.section: (4) Ahaz's worship of the gods of Assyria and his death

paragraphs.text: These two verses were mentioned and explained in (2 Kgs 16:19, 20), and in them we see the end of the wicked Ahaz, who was buried after his death in Jerusalem, and not in the tombs of the righteous kings, his predecessors. The beginning of the revival of King Hezekiah, his reforms and his great works

entries.section: (2) The call to the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Hezekiah began his reforms by repairing the house of the Lord and opening its doors, so that service could be offered in it. His father Ahaz had shut the doors of the house and set up an altar after the pattern of the idols' altar which he had seen in Damascus (2 Kgs 16:10, 11), and had neglected the worship of God.

The repairing of the doors of the house of the Lord means overlaying them with gold, which Hezekiah afterwards stripped off to give to the king of Assyria (2 Kgs 18:16). Hezekiah's goodness appears here in that, at the beginning of his reign, in the first month of the first year of his reign, he began to take care of the house of the Lord, because the beginning of every good thing comes from man's relationship with the Church.

May your attachment to the Holy Sacraments and your relationship with the Church be the center of your life and the most important thing in it, and organize all your concerns so that they do not encroach upon your relationship with the Church and your service in it.

entries.section: (2) The call to the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: King Hezekiah gathered the priests and Levites in the east court of the house of the Lord. These are the servants of the temple who know God's Law and His worship; therefore Hezekiah relied on them to begin his reform by renewing the worship in the temple. And he asked two things of them:

1- That they sanctify themselves, in order to purify their hearts by repentance, and also to complete the procedures of the Law concerning purification, so that they would be worthy to serve the house of the Lord.
2- After they had sanctified themselves, Hezekiah asked them to sanctify the house of the Lord, by the following:
a- Removing the traces of pagan worship.
b- Carrying out a general cleaning, to remove the dust and every remnant of neglect, so that the house of the Lord might be in the most beautiful condition, befitting His great presence.

entries.section: (2) The call to the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Hezekiah comes forward in a spirit of repentance, confessing the sins of the fathers, who were unfaithful to God. For Moses, and after him Joshua, and also Jehoiada the priest, who lived in the days of King Joash, made a covenant, on behalf of the people, with God, that they would live with Him and keep His commandments. But the people of God, whether in the kingdom of Judah in the days of Ahaz, the father of Hezekiah, and the kings before him, or in the kingdom of Israel, had forsaken God and worshipped idols and walked in their evil lusts.

entries.section: (2) The call to the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: In the fathers' neglect of God, they abandoned His worship in His house; for example, the shutting of the porch, in which the people who came to worship God gathered, and the priests also neglected the service in the sanctuary, whether in lighting the lamps in the lampstands, or in offering incense on the golden altar of incense. As for the bronze altar before the sanctuary, they no longer offered burnt offerings to God upon it. Thus the house of God became as though abandoned, lifeless and dark, because they were occupied with the worship of idols.

entries.section: (2) The call to the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Hezekiah reminds the priests and Levites, the religious leaders of the people, that when the fathers in the kingdom of Judah forsook God and worshipped idols, God permitted the nations around them, such as Assyria and Aram and the kingdom of Israel, to trouble them, so they were in anxiety and confusion, until the surrounding nations marveled at their weakness.

entries.section: (2) The call to the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Hezekiah also warns those gathered with him about what happened in the kingdom of Israel, for the Assyrians attacked it and took it into captivity, and the kingdom of Israel came to an end in the days of Ahaz, the father of Hezekiah, since the captivity was in the year 722 B.C., at the end of the reign of Ahaz; that is, only a short time had passed since the captivity when Hezekiah began to reign. Here appears Hezekiah's confession that the cause of all the afflictions that came upon the people of God was their sins. By all this Hezekiah tries to warn the servants of the temple and encourage them, to obtain God's pleasure by being exact in His worship, and to save themselves from God's punishment, which took place in the days of the fathers.

entries.section: (2) The call to the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: In the end Hezekiah showed his clear intention to make a covenant with God, to live before Him with all his heart, keeping His commandments and holding fast to His Law, so that he might escape the divine wrath. And as a leader he encourages his people by this covenant to follow him and worship God.

entries.section: (2) The call to the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: This verse shows the fatherhood of Hezekiah, who was still young in age, for he was twenty-five years old, but he bore a great heart and the responsibility of a king for his people, so he says to them, "My sons," and asks the priests and Levites to take care of their service in the temple, since God chose them from among the people to offer the sacrifices and burnt offerings and to light the lamps and incense before Him.

entries.section: (3) The Levites' cleansing of the temple

paragraphs.text: The chiefs of the three Levite clans were zealous: the Kohathites, the Merarites and the Gershonites. Two from each clan rose up, in addition to two from each of the four clans of the singers: Elizaphan, Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun, so the total was fourteen chiefs. And in honor of them God mentioned each one of them by name in the Holy Bible, because they were moved by Hezekiah's words and were zealous for the service of the house of the Lord.

God notices your love and your care for His worship and service, and all that you do is of great value before Him, however small it may seem in your eyes. This is your opportunity at this age to express your love for Him, after He expressed His love for you on the Cross, and even prepared the Kingdom for you, that you may rejoice with Him forever.

entries.section: (3) The Levites' cleansing of the temple

paragraphs.text: These chiefs felt that Hezekiah's words were based on God's word in His Law given to Moses; therefore they were zealous at once and gathered their brethren the Levites to cleanse the temple.

entries.section: (3) The Levites' cleansing of the temple

paragraphs.text: The brook Kidron: A valley lying southeast of Jerusalem, into which the corpses and refuse coming out of the city used to be thrown and burned there, and it joins the valley of the son of Hinnom, in which a fire burns continually, and from it the word "Gehenna" is taken.

The priests cleansed and cleaned the sanctuary, where none is permitted to enter except the priests. And they brought out all uncleanness and filth to the court of the house of God, where the Levites stand, and they took all the uncleanness, with what they had gathered from the court of the house of the Lord, and carried it to the brook Kidron, where they burned it.

entries.section: (3) The Levites' cleansing of the temple

paragraphs.text: The cleansing of the sanctuary took eight days, from the first day of the first month of Hezekiah's reign to the eighth day; and the cleansing of the court of the house of the Lord and the porch took another eight days, and the carrying of the uncleanness in it to the brook Kidron took another eight days; that is, the cleansing of the house of the Lord and all that is connected with it was completed in sixteen days. This shows the abundance of the uncleanness that was there and the extreme neglect in the days of Ahaz and those before him. On the other hand, it shows the care of the priests and Levites for cleansing the house of the Lord.

entries.section: (3) The Levites' cleansing of the temple

paragraphs.text: After the house of the Lord was cleansed, the chiefs of the priests and Levites entered and announced to King Hezekiah the completion of the cleansing of the house of the Lord and everything in it, whether the altars, or the vessels used in them, and everything that was in the sanctuary and in the court of the house of the Lord.

The young Hezekiah inherited a poor, tattered kingdom far from God, but he did not give up; rather he rose with energy to bring his kingdom back to God. King Hezekiah's love for God appears in that he rose early, because the longings of his heart drove him to pray in the house of the Lord, so he gathered the rulers of his people in his kingdom of Judah and went up to the house of the Lord, because it was built on a hill inside Jerusalem.

Hezekiah was not content with cleansing the house of the Lord, but also took care to sanctify it and to make atonement for the people, by offering sacrifices for himself and for his people. This shows that Hezekiah was not content with grieving over the wrong, but did a positive work to correct the wrongs.

And Hezekiah commanded the priests to offer seven each of bulls, rams, lambs and he goats for the sins of all the people, although the Law provides for offering one bull as a burnt offering (Num 15:24) and one he goat as a sin offering (Lev 16:15). Perhaps Hezekiah felt the greatness of his sins and those of his people, because they had neglected to offer sacrifices for many years in the days of his fathers, who neglected the worship of God; therefore he offered the number seven of the animals. And the number seven represents perfection, since Hezekiah felt the perfection of their sin; therefore he needed a complete atonement.

And when Hezekiah says that these sacrifices are for the kingdom, he means his kingdom, that is, the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and by the sanctuary he means the house of the Lord and all that is in it, while by Judah he means all the people of God; for in the Septuagint Israel is written instead of Judah, that is, he means the people of the two kingdoms, because Hezekiah felt his responsibility for his people who were far away in the kingdom of Israel, who had been scattered in the Assyrian captivity, while the weak among them remained in their cities.

The priests killed the seven bulls, and likewise the rams and the lambs, as burnt offerings before God, and sprinkled their blood on the bronze altar, upon which they offered them. Thus the altar regained its place and burnt offerings went up upon it to please God.

The priests laid their hands on the seven he goats of the sin offering, declaring, on behalf of the people, their sin before God, their neglect of His worship and their disobedience of His commandments, and this was before the king and the people. Then they killed these goats and offered them on the bronze altar, to make atonement for the sins of all the people of God, whether in the kingdom of Judah, or the remnant of the northern kingdom of Israel, or those scattered in captivity, because the Assyrian captivity took place in the days of his father King Ahaz. And Hezekiah is the first king since the division of the kingdom to care for the salvation, not only of the people of his kingdom of Judah, but of the people of all the tribes, and to offer sacrifices for them.

After Hezekiah had cleansed the house of the Lord and sanctified it and offered the sacrifices to make atonement for the people, he was able to arrange the priests and the Levite singers, and they stood in the house of the Lord with the musical instruments to sing the Psalms, as King David and Gad the seer and Nathan the prophet had commanded and arranged. For Hezekiah took care of the order of worship which he had received and which had come down to him from the days of King David, and this shows the importance of holding fast to the holy Tradition, that is, the oral teachings which have come down to us from the days of the Apostles, and all the rites of the Church.
And we see clearly that after offering repentance and obtaining forgiveness, a person can launch out into the praise of God and enjoy His presence.
While the burnt offering was being offered, the singers praised God, and the people worshipped before Him, and the king stood in joy and glorification of God.
Thus Hezekiah restored the rite which the Lord commanded in the days of Moses, which is the offering of the burnt offering morning and evening every day.

After the offering of the sacrifice, the king and all the people bowed down in submission to God and in declaration of their holding fast to His worship, and he promised them that they would live for Him. All this was with the praises raised by the singers, in thanksgiving to God, who gave them the grace of standing before Him.

How beautiful it is for you to be in the Church and take part in the prayers and praises and receive the Holy Mysteries, for it is the greatest thing in existence. Be careful of this, whatever your problems, for this is the pledge of the Kingdom and your help in this life, that you may succeed in all your works.

You have filled your hands to the Lord: You have been sanctified and consecrated to the service of God, after being far from it for many years, and it may be that some of the priests had not begun their service, because they found no opportunity for the priesthood in the days of the former wicked kings.
Of a free heart: A heart full of love for God.

After the people saw the sacrifices which Hezekiah offered, mentioned in (v. 21), they were encouraged to offer sacrifices to God themselves also, especially after Hezekiah announced to them that the priests had sanctified themselves and begun their priestly work. So they offered sacrifices and thank offerings to God, who gave them the grace of worshipping Him in His house, and everyone whose heart was full of love offered burnt offerings to God; for burnt offerings are burned entirely before God and the one who offers them takes nothing of them, and this signifies that everyone whose heart is filled with the love of God is ready to give his whole life to Him. Thus the importance of example appears, for the people learned from Hezekiah, who offered the sacrifices and rose early to the house of the Lord.
